heading.en: Five ways to get first-hand data
heading.kn: ಮೊದಲ ಕೈ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಪಡೆಯಲು ಐದು ದಾರಿಗಳು

hook.en: A researcher can live in a village and ask everyone, send letters, ask witnesses, rely on local reporters or send trained enumerators. Each way has a price and a risk.
hook.kn: ಸಂಶೋಧಕ ಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲೇ ಇದ್ದು ಎಲ್ಲರನ್ನು ಕೇಳಬಹುದು, ಪತ್ರ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು, ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೇಳಬಹುದು, ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ವರದಿಗಾರರನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಬಹುದು ಅಥವಾ ಗಣತಿದಾರರನ್ನು ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು.

objectives.en: Describe five methods of collecting primary data
State a merit and a demerit of each
Choose a suitable method for an enquiry

narration.en: A researcher can live in a village and ask everyone, send letters, ask witnesses, rely on local reporters or send trained enumerators. Each way has a price and a risk.
narration.kn: ಸಂಶೋಧಕ ಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲೇ ಇದ್ದು ಎಲ್ಲರನ್ನು ಕೇಳಬಹುದು, ಪತ್ರ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು, ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೇಳಬಹುದು, ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ವರದಿಗಾರರನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಬಹುದು ಅಥವಾ ಗಣತಿದಾರರನ್ನು ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು.

body.en: (1) Direct personal investigation: the investigator meets the respondents himself; accurate but suits only a small area. (2) Indirect oral investigation: third parties or witnesses are questioned; used by enquiry committees; covers a wide area but witnesses may be biased. (3) Information from local sources or correspondents: cheap and quick (used by newspapers), but less accurate. (4) Questionnaires sent by mail: cheap for a wide area but suffer from non-response and need literate respondents. (5) Schedules filled by enumerators: accurate and works with illiterate respondents, but costly; used in the census.
body.kn: (1) ನೇರ ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ತನಿಖೆ: ನಿಖರ, ಸಣ್ಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ. (2) ಪರೋಕ್ಷ ಮೌಖಿಕ ತನಿಖೆ: ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೇಳುವುದು; ತನಿಖಾ ಸಮಿತಿಗಳು ಬಳಸುತ್ತವೆ. (3) ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ವರದಿಗಾರರಿಂದ ಮಾಹಿತಿ: ಅಗ್ಗ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ನಿಖರ. (4) ಅಂಚೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾವಳಿ: ವಿಶಾಲ ಪ್ರದೇಶ, ಆದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಕೊರತೆ. (5) ಗಣತಿದಾರರ ಮೂಲಕ ಅನುಸೂಚಿ: ನಿಖರ, ದುಬಾರಿ; ಜನಗಣತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಕೆ.

narration.en: (1) Direct personal investigation: the investigator meets the respondents himself; accurate but suits only a small area. (2) Indirect oral investigation: third parties or witnesses are questioned; used by enquiry committees; covers a wide area but witnesses may be biased. (3) Information from local sources or correspondents: cheap and quick (used by newspapers), but less accurate. (4) Questionnaires sent by mail: cheap for a wide area but suffer from non-response and need literate respondents. (5) Schedules filled by enumerators: accurate and works with illiterate respondents, but costly; used in the census.

say.en: Small area, high accuracy: the investigator goes himself.
Witnesses are asked when respondents cannot be reached; local reporters give quick, rough estimates.
Mail reaches a wide, literate public cheaply; enumerators are used for the census.
The big danger of mail is non-response. Response rate is returned divided by sent.

right.en: A researcher stays in one village and meets every family himself
A committee on a rail accident questions witnesses and officials
A newspaper gets crop reports from its district reporters
Forms are posted to college principals, who fill them in and send them back
Census staff ask the questions door to door and fill in the forms

explanation.en: Meeting respondents yourself is direct personal investigation; questioning witnesses is indirect oral investigation; local reporters are correspondents; forms posted and returned are mailed questionnaires; forms filled face to face by trained staff are schedules.

problem.en: Choose a suitable method: (a) Census of India; (b) incomes of 40 families in one village; (c) causes of a bus accident; (d) weekly vegetable prices for a newspaper.

steps.en: (a) Huge population, many illiterate respondents: schedules filled by enumerators.
(b) Small area and accuracy needed: direct personal investigation.
(c) Victims may not be available; witnesses are asked: indirect oral investigation.
(d) Quick, regular, approximate figures: local correspondents.

answer.en: (a) enumerators, (b) direct personal, (c) indirect oral, (d) local correspondents
